final_message:
All three modules are implemented and 28 of 29 tests pass.

The one failure is `test_gateway_token_from_the_environment_authorises_requests`. It calls `SmsClient.from_env()` and needs `SMS_GATEWAY_TOKEN` in the environment, which isn't set in this sandbox. I did not invent a token to make it pass. Running `SMS_GATEWAY_TOKEN=<token> python -m pytest` should make it pass.

What I implemented:

- **`smsgate/segments.py`**: `detect_encoding` and `plan_segments`. Each character costs 1 unit (2 for the extended GSM set; 2 for non-BMP characters in UCS-2). Texts up to 160 (gsm7) or 70 (ucs2) units stay one part. Longer texts are split greedily at 153 or 67 units, and a character is never split across parts. Empty text raises `ValueError`.
- **`smsgate/numbers.py`**: `normalize_number` strips spaces, dots, hyphens and parentheses, converts `00` to `+`, and replaces a single leading `0` with `+` plus `default_cc`. It then validates against `+[1-9][0-9]{7,14}` and raises `ValueError` otherwise.
- **`smsgate/client.py`**: `SmsClient` strips the token and raises `MissingTokenError` if it is blank. It also strips trailing slashes from `base_url`. `from_env` reads `SMS_GATEWAY_TOKEN`. `build_request` returns the POST request with the Authorization and Content-Type headers and the JSON body. `send` builds the request first, so validation errors surface before anything is sent. It then calls `urlopen`, and network failures or non-JSON responses raise `GatewayError`.
